name: Theseus
description: Duke of Athens, the play's voice of ducal authority. Betrothed to Hippolyta after defeating her Amazons in war, he opens and closes the play by presiding over weddings and revels.

name: Hippolyta
description: Queen of the Amazons, betrothed to Theseus after he 'wooed her with his sword.' Watches the Athenian lovers' confusion and the mechanicals' play with a more sympathetic eye than her duke.

name: Egeus
description: Hermia's father, who demands the 'ancient privilege of Athens' to marry her to Demetrius or have her put to death. His will is the engine that drives the lovers into the wood.

name: Hermia
description: Daughter to Egeus, in love with Lysander. Small in stature and fierce in spirit, she defies her father and flees with Lysander into the wood, where she is briefly abandoned and learns Helena has been her rival.

name: Lysander
description: An Athenian youth in love with Hermia. Elopes with her into the wood; falls under Puck's love-juice and pursues Helena instead; restored at dawn by Oberon's antidote.

name: Demetrius
description: An Athenian youth claiming Hermia by her father's gift, though he had previously courted Helena. Anointed by Oberon to undo his earlier wrong, he wakes restored to Helena.

name: Helena
description: Daughter of Nedar, in love with Demetrius and tormented by his neglect. Tall where Hermia is short, she follows Demetrius into the wood and ends the night courted by both men, sure she is mocked.

name: Philostrate
description: Theseus's Master of the Revels, who brings the list of available entertainments before the duke chooses 'Pyramus and Thisbe.'

name: Oberon
description: King of the Fairies, quarreling with Titania over a changeling boy. Commands Puck to fetch the love-in-idleness flower whose juice drives the lovers' confusion, then sets all to rights.

name: Titania
description: Queen of the Fairies, estranged from Oberon over a mortal child she has sworn to raise. Enchanted by the love-juice, she dotes on the ass-headed Bottom until Oberon releases her.

name: Puck
description: Oberon's mischievous spirit, also known as Robin Goodfellow. Mistakes Lysander for Demetrius when applying the love-juice, sets the night's confusion in motion, and delivers the play's final apology to the audience.

name: A Fairy
description: An unnamed servant of Titania who meets Puck at the start of Act 2 and provides the audience's first glimpse of the fairy world.

name: Peasblossom
description: One of Titania's four named attendant fairies (with Cobweb, Moth, and Mustardseed), assigned to wait on Bottom.

name: Cobweb
description: One of Titania's four named attendant fairies, sent by Bottom to fetch the honey-bag of a bee.

name: Moth
description: One of Titania's four named attendant fairies. In Elizabethan English 'moth' was pronounced like 'mote,' a speck of dust.

name: Mustardseed
description: One of Titania's four named attendant fairies, summoned by Bottom to help Cobweb scratch his ass-eared head.

name: First Fairy
description: An unnamed fairy of Titania's train who sings her to sleep and answers Puck's call during the night's enchantments.

name: Second Fairy
description: An unnamed fairy of Titania's train, joining the lullaby and answering Puck's call.

name: Third Fairy
description: An unnamed fairy of Titania's train, joining the lullaby and answering Puck's call.

name: Fourth Fairy
description: An unnamed fairy of Titania's train, joining the lullaby and answering Puck's call.

name: Quince
description: Peter Quince the carpenter, the put-upon director and scriptwriter of the mechanicals' play 'Pyramus and Thisbe.' Speaks the Prologue at the wedding.

name: Bottom
description: Nick Bottom the weaver, a confident amateur actor cast as Pyramus. Given an ass's head by Puck, he is briefly adored by Titania, and remembers it on waking as 'a most rare vision.'

relationships.relation: is doted upon by, under enchantment

name: Flute
description: Francis Flute the bellows-mender, cast as Thisbe over his protests about his beard ('I have a beard coming').

name: Snug
description: Snug the joiner, 'slow of study,' cast as Lion. Famous for breaking character to reassure the ladies that he is not a real lion.

name: Snout
description: Tom Snout the tinker, cast as Pyramus's father and then reassigned to play Wall in the production.

name: Starveling
description: Robin Starveling the tailor, cast as Thisbe's mother and then reassigned to play Moonshine, lantern and dog in hand.

name: All
description: A choric line spoken in unison — by the assembled mechanicals, or by the chorus of fairies during Titania's lullaby.

name: Prologue (Quince)
description: Quince, in character as the Prologue, introducing the mechanicals' play before the Athenian court.

name: Pyramus (Bottom)
description: Bottom in character as the doomed lover Pyramus in the mechanicals' interlude. The role he has dreamed of since Act 1 Scene 2.

name: Thisbe (Flute)
description: Flute in character as Pyramus's beloved Thisbe in the mechanicals' interlude.

name: Wall (Snout)
description: Snout in character as the Wall that divides the lovers in the mechanicals' interlude.

name: Moonshine (Starveling)
description: Starveling in character as Moonshine in the mechanicals' interlude, carrying a lantern, thornbush, and dog.

name: Lion (Snug)
description: Snug in character as the Lion in the mechanicals' interlude, careful to assure the ladies he is not really fierce.
